correctness.rationale: The exact Shankar generating function is correctly specialized to its physical cubic branch. Explicit branch boundary algebra yields the stated h(x), its exact Jacobian yields w(c), and endpoint orders O(x^{-2/3}) and O((27/4-x)^{-1/2}) justify reconstruction by a Cauchy keyhole contour, proving every moment, not only tested coefficients. The polynomial \(64y^3-112y^2+44y+7\) has minimum \(68/27\) on [1/4,1], so the density is positive; generalized Vandermonde positivity establishes strict positivity for all finite Hankel minors. A standalone symbolic program verified the algebra and independently numerically checked moments 0–14; neither finite integration nor finite minor tests is used to infer the universal claim.

evidence: Bostan et al., arXiv:2001.00393, §2 explicitly develops Cauchy/Hankel-contour inversion and gives positive measures for Catalan and Fuss-Catalan sequences.

The motivating B-sequence is not the ternary Fuss-Catalan coefficient: it equals a nonconstant k-dependent factor times the ternary Fuss-Catalan number; positivity does not follow from a theorem about the unmodified sequence.
Shankar 2026 derived B as a rational expression in the ternary-tree generating function yet still posed positivity as an open conjecture.

Górska–Penson, arXiv:1304.6008, proves positive moments for the ordinary d-dimensional Catalan sequence C_d(n), whose d=3 initial values are 1,1,5,42,462 rather than B: 1,1,4,21,121. Its specified even-dimensional extension likewise does not contain this B sequence.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An analytic inversion technique and positive measures for the unmodified Fuss-Catalan sequence provide methods, not a stronger theorem including B. We compute the different jump and verify its sign on the complete support, which cannot be inferred merely from algebraicity or from the known Fuss-Catalan moment law.

value.rationale: Shankar 2026 expressly conjectured Stieltjes positivity for this combinatorially natural lattice-word sequence, presenting evidence only for finite 7-by-7 Hankel matrices. The explicit positive measure closes one entire infinite half of that conjecture, determines exact compact support, yields uniqueness of the measure, and strengthens nonnegative Hankel minors to strict positivity of every minor. This is a motivated infinite-family structural fact rather than a routine numerical extension or a reformulation of a preexisting coefficient formula.
